t.1.16.1: When Viṣṇu had gone to sonship to that great-souled king, the blessed Self-existent Svayambhū spoke these words to all the gods.
t.1.16.2: For Viṣṇu, the valiant one, true to his word, who seeks the welfare of us all, create mighty helpers able to take on any form at will.
t.1.16.3: Sons versed in magic and valiant, equal in swiftness to the speed of the wind, knowers of sound policy, endowed with intelligence, and equal to Viṣṇu in prowess.
t.1.16.4: Beings who cannot be overcome, who know every stratagem, who are endowed with divine bodily strength and possess mastery of all weapons, like those who feed on amṛta.
t.1.16.6: In the bodies of Kiṃnarīs and in the forms of monkey-females, beget sons in the form of monkeys, equal to yourselves in valor.
t.1.16.5: Upon the foremost Apsarases and in the bodies of Gandharva women, upon the maidens of the Yakṣas and Pannagas, and upon the she-bears and Vidyādhara women.
t.1.16.8: The great-souled Ṛṣis, the Siddhas, Vidyādharas and Uragas, and the Cāraṇas too begot heroic sons who roamed the forests.
t.1.16.7: Thus addressed by the Lord, they accepted that command, and in this way they begot sons who had the form of monkeys.
t.1.16.9: Those many thousands who were created, intent on the slaying of Daśagrīva, were heroes of immeasurable strength, valorous, and able to assume any form at will.
t.1.16.10: Those bears, monkeys and gopucchas, resembling elephants and mountains, of great bodies and mighty strength, were born swiftly indeed.
t.1.16.11: Whatever form, attire and prowess each god possessed, to each and every one of them a separate son was born endowed with all of these in full.
t.1.16.12: Some vānaras of esteemed valour were born of female golāṅgūla monkeys, and likewise others were born of female bears and of Kiṃnarīs.
t.1.16.13: All of them fought with rocks as their weapons, all of them battled with trees; all had claws and fangs for weapons, and all were skilled in every kind of missile.
t.1.16.14: They could shake the lords of mountains and split the firmly rooted trees, and with their speed they could agitate the ocean, the lord of rivers.
t.1.16.15: They could split the earth with their feet and leap across the great ocean; they could enter the vault of the sky and even seize the clouds.
t.1.16.16: They should be able to seize even rutting elephants roaming in the forest, and with their roar bring down the crying birds.
t.1.16.17: Of such monkeys, able to take any form at will, great-souled leaders of troops, there were born a hundred hundred-thousands of offspring, and the foremost among the troop leaders in turn begot heroic monkeys.
t.1.16.18: Others, by the thousands, settled on the tablelands of Ṛkṣavant, while still others resorted to mountains of many kinds and to forests.
t.1.16.20: For the sake of aiding Rāma, the earth became covered with those mighty leaders of monkey troops, whose bodies were like masses of clouds and mountains, and whose forms were fearsome to behold.
t.1.16.19: All those lords of the monkeys attended upon the two brothers, Sugrīva, the son of Sūrya, and Vālin, the son of Śakra.
